_comment: The firmware's mel front end (blinky-firmware SharedSpectralAnalysis::computeMelBandsFrom, the onset NN input via getRawMelBands) as a contract (blinky_time#295, #291). blinky-firmware (tests/parity/spec/) and blinky_time (ml-training/spec/) each carry an identical copy of this file and of the golden vectors it names; each repo's CI checks its own side against them, with no source from the other. blinky-firmware checks that 'bands' is MEL_BANDS[], the constants are its own, 'version' is MEL_FRONTEND_VERSION (the number a model header records) and its code still produces the golden mel; blinky_time checks that training's front end (scripts/mel_frontend.py) reproduces the golden mel. A change is a new version: firmware first, then copy both files here. Keys starting with '_' are notes and test data, outside the content digest a dataset records.
num_bins_note: bins 0..127 of the 129-bin rFFT; the Nyquist bin is dropped
bands_note: [startBin, centerBin, endBin], integer FFT bins. Rising edge: bins start..center, weight (b-start)/(center-start), or 1 when center==start. Falling edge: bins center+1..end, weight 1-(b-center)/(end-center). Bins >= num_bins are skipped. The start and end bins carry weight 0. Bands 1 and 2 are identical ({1,2,3}); band 0 is bin 1 alone.
silence_note: band_energy < silence_threshold -> output exactly 0.0, before the log

_golden.format: numpy .npz: 'mags' float32 (frames, num_bins), magnitude frames of rFFT bins 0..num_bins-1; 'mel' float32 (frames, n_mels), the firmware's getRawMelBands() on each frame
_golden.frames_note: silence, flat levels from below the silence threshold to clipping, one bin at a time (each band's support and weights), 24 random log-uniform frames, a kick and a noise burst through the window
_golden.atol_note: any implementation's mel on 'mags' must match 'mel' within atol (float64 against the firmware's float32 agree to ~1e-6)
_golden.reference_note: the firmware itself must still produce 'mel' within reference_atol. Its parity test (blinky-firmware tests/parity/test_mel_contract.py --regenerate) writes the file when the front end changes on purpose, with a new version
